passage: The registration link closed at nine the next morning, and the power had gone out, so the family sat around one lamp in the shop's back room. Jasleen had a pencil and the back of a bill. “Two evenings before camp I'll work the counter till closing,” she said. Her mother tapped the wall calendar. “And during?” “Cousin Thomas can come. He said he's free that fortnight.” Papa raised an eyebrow. “Accounts?” “I'll fill the daily sheet on my phone every night from camp. Ten minutes.” Papa counted on his fingers: two evenings, a cousin, a nightly sheet. “Neither of us gets everything we wanted,” he said. “But nobody loses everything.” Jasleen hugged her mother, then rang Thomas by torchlight.

qa.q: How will Jasleen handle the accounts during camp?
qa.a: She will fill the daily sheet on her phone every night, about ten minutes.

qa.q: What might Jasleen have felt when Papa said nobody loses everything?
qa.a: Relief and gratitude: she hugged her mother and rang her cousin at once.

qa.q: What could the family try if Thomas could not come, and why?
qa.a: They could ask a neighbour's teenager or shorten the shifts, because the aim is to keep the counter covered without dropping the camp.

qa.q: How does the deal look to Thomas?
qa.a: Thomas is being asked to give up a fortnight of free time, so he would want proper notice and clear hours; his ready yes suggests he wants to help.

grounding: A family agrees two evenings of work, a cousin's cover and online accounts so both needs are partly met.
